description: Config-driven rule pack measuring enablement, usage, response validity/relevance and performance posture for Power BI Copilot and Microsoft Fabric data agents. Designed so that AI query generation is narrowly scoped and grounded rather than broad-scanning an unconstrained schema.

extensionPoints.note: Drop additional rule files matching the same rule schema into rules/custom/. The harness merges them by id; a custom rule with an existing id overrides the built-in rule of that id.

blocker.description: AI features cannot function or cannot be trusted at all until fixed. A failed blocker caps overall maturity at Not Ready.

critical.description: Materially wrong answers, security exposure, or severe cost/latency. Fix before broad rollout.

high.description: Frequent ambiguity, degraded relevance, or avoidable capacity burn.

medium.description: Noticeable quality or efficiency loss; fix during hardening.

low.description: Polish and consistency; improves long-run maintainability.

partial.description: Partially met, e.g. applied to some models/agents but not all in scope.

na.description: Out of scope for this estate; removed from both numerator and denominator.

unknown.description: Not yet assessed. Scored as fail but reported separately as assessment debt.

maturityLevels.name: Not Ready
maturityLevels.meaning: Do not expose Copilot or data agents to business users. Blocking enablement or trust gaps present.

maturityLevels.name: Foundational
maturityLevels.meaning: Enabled and technically working, but answers are unreliable and cost/latency is uncontrolled. Pilot with a closed group only.

maturityLevels.name: Operational
maturityLevels.meaning: Scoped and governed for a defined question set. Suitable for a supervised department rollout.

maturityLevels.name: Optimized
maturityLevels.meaning: Grounded, narrow, measured. Answers are repeatable and query cost is bounded. Suitable for broad rollout.

maturityLevels.name: AI-Ready
maturityLevels.meaning: Continuously evaluated against a golden question set with regression gates in the release pipeline.

scoring.areaScore: 100 * sum(ruleScore in area) / sum(maxRuleScore in area, excluding na)
scoring.overallScore: sum(areaScore * areaWeight) / sum(areaWeight of areas with at least one applicable rule)
scoring.gate: If any rule with severity=blocker has result=fail or unknown, overallMaturity is forced to level 0 regardless of numeric score. The numeric score is still reported.

rules.title: Copilot / Azure OpenAI tenant switch is enabled for the intended audience
rules.requirement: The tenant setting 'Users can use Copilot and other features powered by Azure OpenAI' must be enabled, scoped either to the whole organization or to the specific security groups that are in scope for AI.
rules.rationale: This is the master switch. Every downstream Copilot and data agent experience depends on it.

check.how: Fabric Admin Portal > Tenant settings > Copilot and Agent. Record state and the security groups it is scoped to.

rules.remediation: Enable the setting and scope it to the AI pilot security group rather than the entire organization, so that usage and capacity burn stay attributable during rollout.
rules.impactIfViolated: No Copilot or data agent functionality at all.
rules.notes: Microsoft docs are inconsistent on the default state of this switch: the Copilot and Agent admin settings page and the Power BI enablement page describe it as enabled by default, while the data agent tenant settings page lists it as off. Do not assume - read the actual tenant state and record it as evidence.

rules.title: Cross-geo processing switch matches the capacity's region
rules.requirement: If the Fabric capacity is outside the US regions and the EU Data Boundary, the tenant setting 'Data sent to Azure OpenAI can be processed outside your capacity's geographic region, compliance boundary, or national cloud instance' must be enabled, and that decision must be signed off by the data-residency owner.
rules.rationale: Azure OpenAI is deployed in US datacenters and the EU Data Boundary only. UK capacities route to the EU boundary; Australia, Brazil, Canada, India, Asia, Japan, Korea, South Africa, Southeast Asia and UAE route to the US. Without the switch, Copilot simply does not work in those regions.

check.how: Determine the capacity's region, then check the cross-geo processing tenant setting. Record both, plus the residency sign-off reference.
check.expected: enabled when capacity region is outside US and EU Data Boundary

rules.remediation: Either enable cross-geo processing with documented residency approval, or relocate the capacity into a region where Azure OpenAI is served locally.
rules.impactIfViolated: Copilot requests fail in-region; users experience errors rather than degraded answers.

rules.title: Cross-geo storage and conversation-history switches are a deliberate decision
rules.requirement: For tenants outside the EU Data Boundary and US, the settings 'Data sent to Azure OpenAI can be stored outside...' and 'Conversation history stored outside your capacity's geographic region...' must be explicitly decided - enabled with residency approval, or accepted as disabled with the loss of multi-session context understood.
rules.rationale: Conversation history is what gives agentic experiences memory across sessions; it is retained 28 days unless a user deletes it. Leaving these off outside EU/US silently degrades multi-turn quality.

check.how: Record both switch states and the documented decision. Both default to disabled.

rules.remediation: Record the decision in the AI governance register. If disabled, set user expectations that each session starts cold.
rules.impactIfViolated: Agents lose cross-session context; users repeat themselves and blame the agent for forgetting.

limit.description: Conversation history retention when storage is permitted.

rules.title: 'Only show approved items in the standalone Copilot' is enabled once an approval process exists
rules.requirement: Once the organization has a working 'Approved for Copilot' review process, the tenant setting 'Only show approved items in the standalone Copilot in Power BI experience' should be enabled so standalone Copilot searches only curated content.
rules.rationale: This is the single most effective lever against the ad-hoc-scan behaviour: it stops standalone Copilot from ranging across every semantic model in the tenant and restricts it to models that have actually been prepared for AI.

check.how: Check the tenant setting state, and confirm at least one model has been marked Approved for Copilot.

rules.remediation: Stand up the approval review first (see WSP-004), then flip this switch. Enabling it with zero approved items makes standalone Copilot return nothing.
rules.impactIfViolated: Standalone Copilot searches unprepared models and produces confident answers from models nobody has validated.

rules.title: Standalone Copilot experience switch state is intentional
rules.requirement: The setting 'Users can access a standalone, cross-item Copilot in Power BI experience' must be explicitly set on or off with a recorded rationale, not left at whatever the default happens to be.
rules.rationale: Standalone Copilot has the broadest blast radius of any Copilot surface because it is not anchored to one report. It also depends on the parent Azure OpenAI switch and is unavailable in Spain Central, Qatar, India-West and Mexico.

check.how: Record switch state, target groups, and the rationale. Confirm the tenant home region is not one of the unsupported regions.

rules.remediation: Keep it off until model preparation and approval reach Optimized maturity, then enable narrowly.
rules.impactIfViolated: Broad, ungrounded question surface exposed before models are ready.

rules.title: Fabric Copilot capacity designation is configured for cost attribution
rules.requirement: If Copilot cost needs to be isolated from analytical workloads, the setting 'Capacities can be designated as Copilot in Fabric capacities' must be enabled and a dedicated Copilot capacity assigned.
rules.rationale: Copilot consumes the same CU pool as everything else. A dedicated Copilot capacity consolidates AI billing and prevents AI spikes from throttling refreshes and report queries.

check.how: Check the tenant setting, then check whether a capacity is designated and which users or groups are assigned to it.
check.expected: designated capacity or documented decision not to

rules.remediation: Designate a Copilot capacity and assign the AI audience to it, so AI Query operations are separately visible in the Capacity Metrics app.
rules.impactIfViolated: AI consumption is indistinguishable from BI consumption; throttling incidents cannot be attributed.

rules.title: Capacity-level Copilot delegation is reviewed, not just tenant settings
rules.requirement: Delegated tenant settings on each in-scope capacity must be reviewed, because a capacity administrator can enable Copilot at capacity level even where it is disabled at tenant level.
rules.rationale: Reviewing only the tenant page gives a false sense of control. Cross-geo delegation notably does not auto-delegate and must be set per capacity.

check.how: Admin Portal > Capacity settings > each capacity > Delegated tenant settings. Record any capacity that overrides the tenant position.

rules.remediation: Audit every capacity's delegated settings and reconcile overrides against the intended tenant policy.
rules.impactIfViolated: Shadow Copilot enablement on capacities the AI governance team does not know about.

rules.title: Purview DLP and access-restriction policies are evaluated for AI surfaces
rules.requirement: Where the tenant is governed by Microsoft Purview, DLP policies for Fabric Data Warehouse and access-restriction policies for KQL Database, SQL Database and Data Warehouse must be reviewed against the data an agent can reach.
rules.rationale: An agent inherits the user's read access; Purview policies are the layer that prevents an otherwise-authorized query from surfacing regulated content in a chat response.

check.how: List agent data sources, then confirm each has been assessed against active Purview DLP and access-restriction policies.

rules.remediation: Run a Purview policy review as part of agent intake; block sources that carry regulated data without a policy.
rules.impactIfViolated: Regulated data surfaced conversationally with no DLP interception.

rules.title: Tenant setting changes are allowed an hour to propagate before troubleshooting
rules.requirement: The runbook must state that Copilot and data agent tenant settings can take up to one hour to take effect, and that troubleshooting should not begin before that window elapses.
rules.rationale: Most 'Copilot is broken after we enabled it' escalations are impatience. Codifying the wait prevents wasted support cycles and premature setting churn.

check.how: Confirm the enablement runbook documents the propagation delay.

rules.remediation: Add the one-hour propagation note to the enablement runbook and the support script.
rules.impactIfViolated: Settings toggled repeatedly during the propagation window, confusing the audit trail.

rules.title: Capacity meets the minimum paid SKU
rules.requirement: Every workspace hosting a Copilot-enabled model or a data agent must be on a paid Fabric capacity of F2 or higher, or Power BI Premium P1 or higher with Fabric enabled.
rules.rationale: Trial SKUs are not supported for Azure OpenAI access. This is a hard gate, not a performance recommendation.

check.how: Enumerate in-scope workspaces and their assigned capacity SKU. Flag any on trial, PPU-only, or shared capacity.

rules.remediation: Move the workspace to a qualifying paid capacity, or assign users to a Fabric Copilot capacity.
rules.impactIfViolated: Copilot and data agent features are unavailable regardless of tenant settings.

limit.description: Minimum paid capacity SKU; trial SKUs unsupported.

rules.title: Capacity region is supported and consistent across agent and sources
rules.requirement: The data agent's workspace capacity and every data source workspace capacity must be in the same region, and that region must be one where Fabric AI workloads are available.
rules.rationale: Cross-region source binding fails outright - a Lakehouse on North Europe capacity will not serve an agent whose capacity is in France Central. Sovereign clouds are not supported at all.

check.how: For each agent, list the region of its own capacity and of every bound data source's capacity. All must match.
check.expected: identical region across agent and all sources

rules.remediation: Relocate either the agent workspace or the source workspaces so all sit on same-region capacity.
rules.impactIfViolated: Agent creation or query execution fails against the mismatched source.

rules.title: AI Query consumption is monitored in the Capacity Metrics app
rules.requirement: AI Query operations and the LlmPlugin item kind must be actively monitored in the Fabric Capacity Metrics app, with a named owner and a review cadence.
rules.rationale: Data agent requests bill at 100 CU seconds per 1,000 input tokens, 10 CU seconds per 1,000 cached input tokens, and 400 CU seconds per 1,000 output tokens - and the generated SQL/DAX/KQL is billed separately to its own engine on top. Without monitoring, a verbose instruction set silently multiplies cost on every single question.

check.how: Capacity Metrics app, filter to AI Query operations and the LlmPlugin item kind. Confirm a monitoring owner and cadence exist.

rules.remediation: Add AI Query to the capacity review pack; alert on week-over-week growth and on the ratio of output to input tokens.
rules.impactIfViolated: Unbounded AI spend and eventual capacity-wide throttling that takes refreshes down with it.

limit.description: Data agent AI Query consumption rates. Query execution against the source engine is billed separately.

rules.title: Throttling risk from AI workloads is assessed against the SKU
rules.requirement: Expected peak AI request volume must be modelled against the capacity's daily CU budget, and the result recorded, before broad rollout.
rules.rationale: Data agent operations run as background jobs which smooth peaks, but once capacity is exhausted all operations shut down - not just AI. An F64 carrying 1,536 CU hours per day supports on the order of 13,800 requests per day before exhaustion; that number falls fast as instructions and conversation history grow.

check.how: Record the SKU, its daily CU hours, the modelled average tokens per request, and the derived request ceiling. Compare against forecast adoption.

rules.remediation: Model it explicitly, then either size the capacity for the forecast or cap the audience until instruction and schema trimming brings per-request tokens down.
rules.impactIfViolated: AI adoption success takes down unrelated Fabric workloads on the same capacity.

rules.title: Private Link and closed-network constraints are checked
rules.requirement: Confirm that in-scope capacities do not depend on Private Link or closed-network configurations that are unsupported for Copilot.
rules.rationale: Copilot is not supported behind Private Link or closed networks. Discovering this after a rollout announcement is expensive.

check.how: Check tenant and workspace networking configuration for Private Link / closed-network enforcement.

rules.remediation: Carve the AI-enabled workspaces out of the Private Link enforcement scope, or accept that Copilot is unavailable there.
rules.impactIfViolated: Copilot silently unavailable despite every switch appearing correct.

rules.title: Workspace outbound access protection boundaries are understood for agents
rules.requirement: Where workspace outbound access protection is in force, the permitted external endpoints must be documented and confirmed sufficient for the agent's data sources.
rules.rationale: Agents operate inside the workspace outbound access protection boundary; an administrator's endpoint allowlist directly determines what the agent can reach.

check.how: Record outbound access protection state and the allowlisted endpoints for each agent workspace.

rules.remediation: Reconcile the endpoint allowlist with the agent's bound sources before go-live.
rules.impactIfViolated: Intermittent, hard-to-diagnose source failures.

rules.title: AI-enabled workspaces are an explicit, enumerated set
rules.requirement: There must be a maintained register of which workspaces are in scope for Copilot and data agents, rather than AI being implicitly available wherever capacity happens to be assigned.
rules.rationale: Scope control is the foundation of every other rule in this pack. You cannot tune what you have not bounded.

check.how: Confirm a register exists, is current within the last quarter, and names an owner per workspace.

rules.remediation: Publish the register and review it at each capacity review.
rules.impactIfViolated: AI surface expands invisibly; assessment results go stale immediately.

rules.title: Copilot cannot be enabled per workload - the audience decision is all-or-nothing
rules.requirement: The rollout plan must account for the fact that enabling Copilot in a capacity for a user or security group grants that group all Copilot workloads and experiences; it cannot be enabled for one experience only.
rules.rationale: Teams frequently plan a 'Copilot for Power BI only' pilot that is not technically achievable. The control point is the audience, not the workload.

check.how: Confirm the rollout plan controls exposure by security group and capacity assignment, not by workload selection.

rules.remediation: Rewrite the rollout plan around security groups and dedicated capacities.
rules.impactIfViolated: Users reach Copilot experiences over unprepared workloads that were never in the pilot scope.

rules.title: Staging, development and sandbox workspaces are excluded from AI capacity
rules.requirement: Development, staging and personal sandbox workspaces must not sit on capacity where Copilot is enabled for business users.
rules.rationale: Half-built models with placeholder measures and unhidden technical columns are exactly the content that teaches users not to trust Copilot.

check.how: Cross-reference the workspace register against capacity assignment; flag any dev/test workspace on a Copilot-enabled capacity accessible to business users.

rules.remediation: Move non-production workspaces to a separate capacity or restrict the Copilot security group to production workspace members.
rules.impactIfViolated: Users get answers from unfinished models and lose confidence permanently.

rules.title: 'Approved for Copilot' is applied through a real review, not by default
rules.requirement: Every semantic model marked 'Approved for Copilot' must have passed a documented review covering schema scoping, descriptions, verified answers and a golden-question test pass.
rules.rationale: Approval is the trust signal shown to users; unapproved models display a warning advising users to inspect results and contact the owner. Rubber-stamping approval destroys the signal's value.

check.how: For each approved model, confirm a review record exists with a date, reviewer, and golden-question pass rate.

rules.remediation: Define the approval checklist from this rule pack and gate the flag behind it.
rules.impactIfViolated: The approval badge becomes noise and users cannot tell prepared models from unprepared ones.

rules.title: Reports, dashboards and apps cannot be approved - only semantic models
rules.requirement: Governance documentation must state that there is currently no way to mark a report, dashboard or app as approved for Copilot; only semantic models carry the flag.
rules.rationale: Teams design approval workflows around reports and then find the flag does not exist, leaving the process half-implemented.

check.how: Confirm the governance doc reflects the model-only scope of approval.

rules.remediation: Anchor the approval process on semantic models and treat report quality as a separate control.
rules.impactIfViolated: Approval process design churn.

rules.title: Semantic model description is populated for discovery
rules.requirement: Each in-scope semantic model must have a populated description in model settings that names the subject areas, key entities and the questions it is meant to answer.
rules.rationale: Descriptions feed the Search grounding path, which is how standalone Copilot decides which model to use for a question. A blank description makes the model effectively invisible or, worse, picked at random.

check.how: Read the model description for every in-scope model; flag empty, default, or single-word values.

rules.remediation: Write a description covering tables, measures, relationships and intended audience, using distinct keywords rather than generic phrasing.
rules.impactIfViolated: Standalone Copilot routes questions to the wrong model.

rules.title: Report descriptions are populated where reports are part of the AI surface
rules.requirement: Reports exposed to Copilot should carry a description in File > Settings that provides natural-language context for data discovery.
rules.rationale: Report descriptions contribute to discovery and to the report summary experience.

check.how: Sample in-scope reports and check for a populated description.

rules.remediation: Add a one-to-two sentence description naming the analysis and its dimensions.
rules.impactIfViolated: Weaker discovery and less useful report summaries.

rules.title: An AI data schema is explicitly defined for every in-scope semantic model
rules.requirement: Every semantic model exposed to Copilot or bound to a data agent must have an AI data schema defined through Prep data for AI, rather than defaulting to the full model surface.
rules.rationale: This is the primary control against the ad-hoc-SQL-server behaviour. The DAX generation tool uses only the AI data schema. If you never define one, the generator reasons over everything you own.

check.how: Inspect the model's LSDL / AI data schema definition. Confirm a curated selection exists and is narrower than the full object list.
check.expected: defined and narrower than full model

rules.remediation: Open Prep data for AI > Simplify the data schema and deselect every field not required by the intended question set.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator considers every table, column and measure on every question - maximum latency, maximum token cost, maximum ambiguity.

rules.title: Model entity count stays within the 1,000-entity indexing ceiling
rules.requirement: The combined count of tables and columns in the model should stay at or below 1,000 entities, or the AI data schema must reduce the exposed surface to below that ceiling.
rules.rationale: Power BI indexes a maximum of 1,000 model entities (tables and columns combined) for instance-value search. Beyond that, columns go unindexed and value-based filtering silently degrades.

check.how: Count tables plus columns via INFO.TABLES()/INFO.COLUMNS() or a VPAX extract. Compare against 1000.

rules.remediation: Trim the model, or narrow the AI data schema so the AI-visible entity count is well under the ceiling. Aim materially below 1,000, not at it.
rules.impactIfViolated: Columns are skipped during indexing; Copilot cannot resolve filter values it should be able to find.

limit.description: Maximum model entities indexed for instance values.

rules.title: Instance-value indexing stays within the 5 million value ceiling
rules.requirement: The total indexed instance values across the model must stay under 5 million, and high-cardinality columns must be excluded from the AI data schema where they are not needed for filtering.
rules.rationale: Indexing stops at 5 million instance values. When the next column would push the total over, Power BI skips that column entirely - and it may be a column that matters. A single high-cardinality key can consume the budget and starve every column after it.

check.how: Estimate distinct-value counts per AI-visible column (APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT or COLUMNSTATISTICS) and sum. Compare against 5,000,000.

rules.remediation: Deselect surrogate keys, GUIDs, free-text notes and transaction identifiers from the AI data schema. Keep the columns users actually name in questions.
rules.impactIfViolated: Arbitrary columns silently unindexed; value filters fail unpredictably and look like model bugs.

limit.description: Upper bound on indexed instance values; a column that would exceed it is skipped entirely.

rules.title: Filterable text values are under 100 characters
rules.requirement: Columns intended for value-based filtering by Copilot must contain values shorter than 100 characters.
rules.rationale: Text values of 100 characters or more are not indexed. Long descriptive strings will never be matched by a user's natural-language filter no matter how the question is phrased.

check.how: For each AI-visible text column, compute MAX(LEN(column)). Flag any column used for filtering whose values reach 100 characters.

rules.remediation: Split long text into a short filterable code or category column plus a long descriptive column, and expose only the short one to the AI data schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Users filter on a value that visibly exists in the report and Copilot insists it cannot find it.

limit.description: Text values at or above this length are not indexed.

rules.title: Copilot Diagnostics shows no AgentSchemaReduced warning
rules.requirement: Copilot Diagnostics must not report 'AgentSchemaReduced' for in-scope models under representative questions.
rules.rationale: AgentSchemaReduced means the schema was too large for Copilot to render and Copilot automatically cut it down - by its own choice, not yours. Whatever it dropped is invisible to the generator and you did not decide what went.

check.how: Run the golden question set and inspect Copilot Diagnostics warnings for AgentSchemaReduced.

rules.remediation: Reduce the AI data schema yourself until the warning clears, so schema reduction is a deliberate curation decision rather than an automatic truncation.
rules.impactIfViolated: Silent, uncontrolled loss of schema; answers omit data that exists and nobody can explain why.

rules.title: Surrogate keys and relationship identifiers are removed from the AI schema
rules.requirement: Unique identifier columns used only to define relationships must be deselected from the AI data schema.
rules.rationale: Documented explicitly as a field type to deselect. Keys carry no business meaning, add cardinality against the indexing budget, and invite the generator to join or group on them.

check.how: List AI-visible columns whose names match key patterns (ID, Key, SK, GUID, Code suffixes) and confirm exclusion unless deliberately kept.

rules.remediation: Deselect them in Simplify the data schema. Relationships still work; the generator just stops seeing the keys.
rules.impactIfViolated: Grouping by meaningless identifiers, wasted index budget, and joins the generator invents rather than follows.

rules.title: Sort-order and helper columns are removed from the AI schema
rules.requirement: Sort-by columns such as Month (Sort Order) or Day (Sort Order), and other presentation helper columns, must be deselected from the AI data schema.
rules.rationale: Called out explicitly as fields to deselect. They duplicate a real attribute in numeric form, so the generator has two plausible columns for one concept and picks wrong roughly half the time.

check.how: Identify columns used as Sort By Column targets and confirm they are excluded from the AI schema.

rules.remediation: Deselect all sort-order columns. Sorting behaviour in visuals is unaffected.
rules.impactIfViolated: Answers grouped by 1..12 instead of month names; user trust erodes on cosmetic-looking errors.

rules.title: Archived, staging and audit tables are excluded
rules.requirement: Archived, staging, audit and unrelated tables must be excluded from both the AI data schema and any data agent object selection.
rules.rationale: Explicit guidance for data agent configuration: select only the tables, columns, views and functions needed for the intended questions. Staging tables are the classic source of near-duplicate results.

check.how: Review the AI-visible table list against the intended question set; flag any table that no in-scope question needs.

rules.remediation: Remove them from selection. If they must stay in the model for lineage, hide them and exclude them from the AI schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator queries a staging copy and returns numbers that do not tie to any published report.

rules.title: AI data schema is scoped to a declared question set
rules.requirement: Each AI data schema must be traceable to a written statement of the question scope the model is meant to serve, and every included object must be justified by at least one question in that scope.
rules.rationale: 'Select only relevant objects based on the data agent's question scope to reduce ambiguity and latency.' Without a declared scope, inclusion decisions are arbitrary and the schema only ever grows.

check.how: Confirm a question-scope document exists per model/agent and that schema inclusions map to it.

rules.remediation: Write the scope statement first, derive the schema from it, and reject additions that no scoped question requires.
rules.impactIfViolated: Schema sprawl returns within two release cycles and undoes every other tuning effort.

rules.title: Data agent object selection matches the model's AI data schema
rules.requirement: For a semantic model bound to a data agent, the tables selected in the data agent must be the same tables defined in the model's Prep for AI AI data schema.
rules.rationale: Stated as a direct consistency rule. Divergence means the agent exposes objects the DAX generator was never configured to reason about.

check.how: Diff the agent's selected object list against the model's AI data schema. The sets must match.

rules.remediation: Reconcile the two selections and add a check to the release process so they cannot drift.
rules.impactIfViolated: Objects visible to the agent but absent from the generation schema produce failed or nonsensical DAX.

rules.title: Dependent objects of selected measures are included in the schema
rules.requirement: When a measure is included in the AI data schema, every object it depends on must also be included.
rules.rationale: Explicit dependency rule; Semantic Link Labs' get_measure_dependencies is the recommended way to enumerate them. A measure whose dependencies were trimmed away fails at query time.

check.how: Run get_measure_dependencies (Semantic Link Labs) across AI-visible measures and confirm every dependency is also AI-visible.

rules.remediation: Add the missing dependencies, or drop the measure from the schema if its dependencies must stay hidden.
rules.impactIfViolated: Generated DAX references objects the generator believes exist and the query errors.

rules.title: Hidden fields are not silently relied upon
rules.requirement: Any field that Copilot must be able to use has to be visible; hidden measures and columns are excluded from grounding and must not appear in verified answers.
rules.rationale: Hidden fields are excluded from grounding data, and verified answers referencing hidden columns simply do not work. Teams routinely hide a column for report tidiness and then wonder why Copilot cannot answer about it.

check.how: List objects referenced by verified answers and by the question scope, and confirm none are hidden.
check.expected: no hidden objects in AI scope

rules.remediation: Unhide the fields Copilot needs, or rewrite the verified answer against visible equivalents.
rules.impactIfViolated: Verified answers fail silently and Copilot claims data it can see in reports does not exist.

rules.title: Private tables are understood to be entirely invisible to Copilot
rules.requirement: Tables marked private must be documented as fully excluded from all Copilot grounding, and no AI capability may depend on them.
rules.rationale: Copilot ignores private tables entirely across both the data-question and DAX query view paths. This is a useful deliberate exclusion mechanism, but a trap when unintentional.

check.how: List tables marked private and confirm no in-scope question depends on them.

rules.remediation: Use the private flag deliberately to fence off sensitive or technical tables; unmark any table Copilot legitimately needs.
rules.impactIfViolated: Unexplainable gaps in Copilot's knowledge of the model.

rules.title: Duplicate field names across tables are eliminated or disambiguated
rules.requirement: The AI-visible schema must not contain identically named fields in multiple tables unless each carries a description that distinguishes it.
rules.rationale: Called out directly: 'Name' in a Customer table versus a Store table forces the generator to guess. Ambiguity at schema level cannot be recovered by a better prompt.

check.how: Group AI-visible column and measure names; flag any name appearing in more than one table.

rules.remediation: Rename to Customer Name / Store Name, or add distinguishing descriptions to each.
rules.impactIfViolated: Roughly random field selection on any question naming the ambiguous term.

rules.title: Instance-value reindexing cadence is understood and accounted for
rules.requirement: The team must document the reindexing behaviour that applies to each model type and set user expectations accordingly.
rules.rationale: Import models reindex on manual or scheduled refresh, but only when Copilot or Q&A has been used in the last 14 days. DirectQuery and Direct Lake reindex when the index is older than 24 hours under the same 14-day activity condition, with COLUMNSTATISTICS cached for 7 days. A model nobody has asked a question of for two weeks stops being reindexed.

check.how: Confirm the operations runbook records the reindexing rules per model type and the 14-day activity dependency.

rules.remediation: Document it, and for low-traffic but important models schedule a periodic synthetic question to keep the model within the activity window.
rules.impactIfViolated: Stale instance values produce filter misses that look like data errors.

rules.title: DirectQuery indexing constraints are accepted or mitigated
rules.requirement: For DirectQuery models, confirm the source supports APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT and accept that indexing occurs at most once per 24 hours unless the model is republished.
rules.rationale: Only columns from sources supporting APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT are indexed at all. A failed underlying refresh leaves a stale index until the next successful one.

check.how: For each DirectQuery model, record source support for APPROXIMATEDISTINCTCOUNT and the observed index age.

rules.remediation: Where the source does not support it, consider Import or Direct Lake for the AI-facing model.
rules.impactIfViolated: Value filtering effectively unavailable on DirectQuery models against unsupported sources.

rules.title: Prep for AI changes are given time to propagate before re-testing
rules.requirement: Test cycles must allow up to 24 hours for Prep for AI changes to affect Copilot results, typically within an hour, with the longer tail on models that have many attached reports.
rules.rationale: Re-testing five minutes after a change and concluding the change did nothing leads to thrashing the configuration.

check.how: Confirm the test procedure documents the propagation window.

rules.remediation: Build the wait into the evaluation cadence; batch configuration changes rather than tuning one setting at a time.
rules.impactIfViolated: Configuration churn and false conclusions about which settings help.

limit.description: Maximum propagation time for Prep for AI changes; usually within one hour.

rules.title: Prep for AI edits deployed via Git or pipelines are followed by a refresh
rules.requirement: After deploying LSDL or Prep for AI changes through Git integration or deployment pipelines, the model must be refreshed in the Power BI service to sync the changes.
rules.rationale: Explicit requirement. Import models must be refreshed; DirectQuery and Direct Lake models must be refreshed but only once a day. Skipping this leaves production running the previous AI configuration while source control says otherwise.

check.how: Confirm the deployment pipeline includes a post-deployment refresh step for AI-configured models.

rules.remediation: Add the refresh to the release pipeline and verify the AI configuration post-deployment rather than assuming it landed.
rules.impactIfViolated: Deployed AI configuration silently inactive in production.

rules.title: Connection type is supported for Desktop-based Prep for AI authoring
rules.requirement: Where Prep for AI is authored in Power BI Desktop, the model must use Import, DirectQuery or local Composite mode.
rules.rationale: Power BI Desktop supports only those connection types for Prep data for AI. All model types can use the features in the Power BI service, so the constraint is on where you author, not where you consume.

check.how: Record the connection type of each model and where its AI configuration is authored.

rules.remediation: Author Prep for AI in the service for model types Desktop does not support.
rules.impactIfViolated: Prep for AI unavailable in Desktop and the team assumes the feature is broken.

rules.title: Data agent stays within the five data source limit and uses the minimum needed
rules.requirement: A data agent must be bound to no more than five data sources, and to the fewest sources that its question scope actually requires.
rules.rationale: Five sources is a hard cap in any combination across Lakehouses, Warehouses, semantic models, KQL databases, mirrored databases, ontologies and Microsoft Graph. Every additional source widens the routing decision the agent has to make on every question.

check.how: Count bound data sources per agent and compare against the intended question scope.

rules.remediation: Split broad agents into several narrowly scoped agents rather than binding more sources to one.
rules.impactIfViolated: At the cap, source routing errors dominate; beyond it, configuration is rejected.

rules.title: Lakehouse content is exposed as tables, not files
rules.requirement: Data intended for agent consumption from a Lakehouse must be registered as tables; standalone files are not accessible.
rules.rationale: Agents access only Lakehouse tables, not standalone CSV or JSON files unless those are ingested as tables. Unstructured formats such as .pdf, .docx and .txt are unsupported outright.

check.how: For each Lakehouse source, confirm the required data is registered as tables.

rules.remediation: Ingest the files as Delta tables before binding the Lakehouse to the agent.
rules.impactIfViolated: The agent cannot see data the user can see in OneLake.

rules.title: Model follows a star schema with distinct fact and dimension tables
rules.requirement: AI-facing semantic models must use a star schema with clearly separated fact and dimension tables; flat denormalized tables and pivoted structures must be avoided.
rules.rationale: Named as the primary structural pitfall: non-star schemas make efficient DAX harder to write correctly, so the generator produces inefficient or wrong queries. This is the single largest structural driver of the broad-scan behaviour.

check.how: Review the relationship graph. Flag snowflaked chains, fact-to-fact relationships, and wide flat tables carrying both measures and descriptive attributes.

rules.remediation: Refactor into conformed dimensions and narrow fact tables. Unpivot wide tables so each row is one observation.
rules.impactIfViolated: Inefficient generated DAX, longer scans, higher CU burn per question, and lower answer accuracy.

rules.title: Relationships are defined with explicit, correct cardinality
rules.requirement: Every relationship between AI-visible tables must exist and declare the correct cardinality - one-to-many, many-to-one, or many-to-many - and the correct filter direction.
rules.rationale: Clear relationships with specified cardinality are a stated requirement. Missing or wrong relationships force the generator to invent joins, which is where fabricated numbers come from.

check.how: Enumerate relationships via INFO.RELATIONSHIPS(). Flag missing joins between AI-visible fact and dimension tables, and any many-to-many not deliberately intended.

rules.remediation: Define the missing relationships and correct cardinality. Replace incidental many-to-many with a bridge dimension.
rules.impactIfViolated: Cross-joins, inflated totals, and answers that cannot be reconciled to any report.

rules.title: Ambiguous relationship paths are eliminated
rules.requirement: The model must not contain ambiguous relationship paths between AI-visible tables.
rules.rationale: Explicitly listed among the practices to follow. Where two paths connect the same tables, the generator's choice is not predictable and neither are the results.

check.how: Trace the relationship graph for multiple active paths between any two AI-visible tables.
check.expected: single active path per table pair

rules.remediation: Deactivate redundant relationships and expose the alternate path through an explicit measure using USERELATIONSHIP.
rules.impactIfViolated: Same question, different answer, depending on the path chosen.

rules.title: Role-playing relationships are marked inactive and surfaced through measures
rules.requirement: Role-playing dimension relationships must be marked inactive where appropriate, with active/inactive state clearly specified.
rules.rationale: Direct guidance to clearly specify active and inactive relationships and mark role-playing relationships inactive when appropriate.

check.how: For dimensions related more than once to a fact, confirm exactly one active relationship and named measures for the inactive roles.
check.expected: one active, roles exposed via measures

rules.remediation: Create measures such as Sales by Ship Date using USERELATIONSHIP, and name them so the role is obvious.
rules.impactIfViolated: Date-based questions silently resolve against the wrong date role.

rules.title: A marked date table with hierarchies exists
rules.requirement: The model must contain a dedicated date dimension with a logical drill hierarchy - Year > Quarter > Month > Day - and it must be marked as the date table.
rules.rationale: Hierarchies for drill-down are a stated structural requirement, and time intelligence in generated DAX depends on a proper date table.

check.how: Confirm a date table exists, is marked as such, is contiguous, and exposes a Year/Quarter/Month/Day hierarchy.

rules.remediation: Add and mark a conformed date dimension; remove auto date/time tables that clutter the AI-visible schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Time-intelligence questions fail or return wrong periods - the most common category of user-facing Copilot error.

rules.title: Ambiguous date columns carry explicit default guidance
rules.requirement: Where a model exposes several date columns - Order Date, Ship Date, Due Date - AI instructions or verified answers must state which is the default for each question type.
rules.rationale: Called out as a specific pitfall: multiple date columns require clear guidance or the AI is confused. Guidance is the fix, not removal.

check.how: Count AI-visible date columns; if more than one, confirm AI instructions name the default and the conditions for using the others.

rules.remediation: Add an explicit line to AI instructions, for example: unless the user names a date type, use Order Date.
rules.impactIfViolated: Revenue questions answered on ship date; the numbers look plausible and are wrong.

rules.title: Fact and dimension tables are explicitly named
rules.requirement: Tables should be named so their role is unmistakable - FactSales, FactTransactions, DimProduct, DimCustomer - or follow an equivalent consistent convention.
rules.rationale: Explicit naming guidance. Role clarity in the name reduces the reasoning the generator must do before it can plan a query.

check.how: Review AI-visible table names for a consistent, role-revealing convention.

rules.remediation: Adopt one convention and apply it uniformly. Consistency matters more than which convention you pick.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator misclassifies a dimension as a fact and aggregates attributes.

rules.title: Unused tables, columns and measures are removed
rules.requirement: Objects not required by any report or by the AI question scope must be removed from the model.
rules.rationale: Model bloat is named directly: remove unnecessary columns, tables and measures to reduce noise for the DAX generation tool. Every unused object is a candidate the generator must rule out.

check.how: Use the Semantic Model Memory Analyzer or a VPAX extract to identify unreferenced objects.

rules.remediation: Delete them, or at minimum hide and exclude them from the AI data schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Higher token cost per question and more ways for the generator to go wrong.

rules.title: Disconnected and field-parameter tables are limited
rules.requirement: Disconnected tables, including field parameter tables, must be minimized in the AI-visible schema and documented where retained.
rules.rationale: Named as an unsupported complex pattern that may cause unexpected results, alongside currency conversion patterns.

check.how: List AI-visible tables with no relationships; confirm each is deliberate and documented.

rules.remediation: Exclude field parameter tables from the AI data schema; they are a report interactivity device, not a semantic concept.
rules.impactIfViolated: Unpredictable results on any question that touches the disconnected table.

rules.title: Currency conversion patterns are flagged as unsupported
rules.requirement: Models implementing currency conversion must document that this pattern is not reliably supported and constrain the question scope accordingly.
rules.rationale: Currency conversion is explicitly listed among complex patterns that may cause unexpected results.

check.how: Identify currency conversion logic and confirm the limitation is documented and tested.

rules.remediation: Pre-compute reporting-currency measures and expose only those to the AI schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Currency-denominated answers are wrong in ways that are hard to spot.

rules.title: Explicit measures exist for every metric users will ask about
rules.requirement: Every business metric within the question scope must be implemented as an explicit DAX measure.
rules.rationale: Explicit measures are required; implicit measures lead to unpredictable results. If the metric is not a measure, the generator has to invent the aggregation.

check.how: Map each metric in the question scope to a named measure. Flag any metric with no measure.

rules.remediation: Create the measures, name them the way the business names them, and describe them.
rules.impactIfViolated: Invented aggregations that do not match the organization's official definition.

rules.title: Implicit measures are suppressed on AI-visible numeric columns
rules.requirement: Numeric columns in the AI schema must not rely on implicit aggregation where an explicit measure is the intended answer.
rules.rationale: Implicit measures are named as a pitfall producing unpredictable results. A raw numeric column adjacent to a proper measure gives the generator a wrong-but-available option.

check.how: For AI-visible numeric columns, confirm either an explicit measure covers the metric and the raw column is excluded, or the column's default summarization is deliberately set.

rules.remediation: Exclude raw fact numeric columns from the AI schema once explicit measures exist.
rules.impactIfViolated: SUM of a raw column returned where a ratio or filtered measure was correct.

rules.title: Default summarization is set correctly on numeric columns
rules.requirement: Every AI-visible numeric column must have a deliberate default summarization - Sum, Average or None - rather than the inherited default.
rules.rationale: Stated requirement, to prevent unintended aggregations. Averaging a ratio column or summing a year is the classic failure.

check.how: Read the summarizeBy property for AI-visible numeric columns. Flag ratio, percentage, year and key columns not set to None.
check.expected: deliberate summarizeBy on every numeric column

rules.remediation: Set summarizeBy to None on identifiers, years and ratios; set Sum or Average deliberately elsewhere.
rules.impactIfViolated: Summed percentages and averaged keys presented as fact.

rules.title: Helper and intermediate measures are excluded from the AI schema
rules.requirement: Only measures that calculate an actual business metric may be AI-visible; helper measures and intermediate objects used for report interactivity must be excluded.
rules.rationale: Direct instruction. Including unnecessary measures increases noise and decreases accuracy.

check.how: Classify every AI-visible measure as business metric or helper; flag helpers.

rules.remediation: Hide helper measures and exclude them from the AI data schema; keep them in a clearly named technical display folder.
rules.impactIfViolated: Answers built on formatting or selection-state helpers that were never meant to be reported.

rules.title: Near-duplicate measures are eliminated or clearly differentiated
rules.requirement: The AI schema must not expose several measures meaning approximately the same thing - Total Sales, Sales Amount, Revenue - unless each carries a description that makes the distinction explicit.
rules.rationale: Named as a pitfall creating ambiguity for DAX generation. This is one of the most common causes of two users getting two different numbers for the same question.

check.how: Cluster AI-visible measure names by semantic similarity; review each cluster for genuine distinction.

rules.remediation: Keep one canonical measure per concept. Where variants are genuinely needed, encode the distinction in the name and describe it.
rules.impactIfViolated: Inconsistent answers to the same business question, which is the fastest route to losing executive trust.

rules.title: Measures are named in business language, not technical shorthand
rules.requirement: Measure and column names must be descriptive business terms - Average Customer Rating rather than AvgRating, Total Revenue rather than TR_AMT, Sales Region rather than DIM_GEO_01.
rules.rationale: Stated with these exact examples. Abbreviations and acronyms increase error probability, and non-descriptive naming leaves the DAX tool with no context at all.

check.how: Scan AI-visible object names for abbreviations, underscores, all-caps tokens and source-system prefixes.

rules.remediation: Rename in the semantic layer. Source-system names belong in Power Query, not in the AI-visible model.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator has no basis for mapping a user's words to your fields.

rules.title: Commonly requested measures are pre-built rather than left to generation
rules.requirement: Frequently requested calculations - YTD, month-over-month growth, prior-year comparison, run rate - must exist as measures instead of relying on the generator to compose them.
rules.rationale: Guidance to include commonly requested measures users are likely to need, with YTD Sales and MoM Growth given as examples. Pre-built beats generated every time on both accuracy and cost.

check.how: Compare the top question patterns against the measure inventory; flag common patterns with no backing measure.

rules.remediation: Build the top time-intelligence and comparison measures explicitly. Each one removes a whole class of generation errors.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator writes time intelligence from scratch on every question, slowly and sometimes wrongly.

rules.title: Business KPIs are defined in the model
rules.requirement: Business-relevant KPIs such as ROI, CAC and LTV should be defined as measures where they are part of the question scope.
rules.rationale: Stated as a requirement with these examples. A KPI the business talks about but the model does not contain is a guaranteed hallucination opportunity.

check.how: Compare the business KPI catalogue to the measure inventory.

rules.remediation: Implement the KPIs with the official definitions and describe the calculation basis.
rules.impactIfViolated: Users ask for a named KPI and receive an approximation the generator assembled.

rules.title: Calculation groups carry item names in the description
rules.requirement: Every calculation group must have a description that lists and explains its calculation items, within the first 200 characters.
rules.rationale: Copilot struggles to use calculation groups; the documented mitigation is to include the calculation item names in the description, which is truncated at 200 characters.

check.how: For each calculation group, confirm the description names the items and that the essential content sits in the first 200 characters.

rules.remediation: Front-load the item names, then any explanation. Anything past character 200 is not read.
rules.impactIfViolated: Calculation groups are effectively invisible and time-intelligence answers ignore them.

rules.title: DAX comments are not used to convey meaning to Copilot
rules.requirement: Semantic context must live in descriptions, not in DAX comments.
rules.rationale: Comments in DAX expressions are explicitly excluded from grounding data. Teams document measures in comments and assume Copilot reads them.

check.how: Sample measures with substantial comment blocks and confirm the same context exists in the description.

rules.remediation: Move the business meaning into the description; keep comments for maintainers.
rules.impactIfViolated: Carefully documented measures that Copilot understands no better than undocumented ones.

rules.title: Newer DAX functions are used cautiously in AI-facing models
rules.requirement: Where a model relies on recently introduced DAX functions or syntax, the team must test AI behaviour against those measures specifically.
rules.rationale: Copilot has limited training data for newer DAX functions and syntax and may produce mistakes with them.

check.how: Identify measures using recent DAX functions and include them in the golden question set.

rules.remediation: Wrap the newer logic in a stable named measure so the generator references rather than rewrites it.
rules.impactIfViolated: Generation errors concentrated in the newest parts of the model.

rules.title: Variable-heavy measures are validated for filter and grouping behaviour
rules.requirement: Measures making heavy use of DAX variables must be tested, because Copilot may inappropriately filter or group on already-declared variables.
rules.rationale: Named as a specific known failure mode.

check.how: Include variable-heavy measures in the golden question set and inspect the generated DAX.

rules.remediation: Simplify the public-facing measure and push variable complexity into helper measures excluded from the AI schema.
rules.impactIfViolated: Subtly wrong filter context in generated queries.

rules.title: Data types are correct and consistent across tables
rules.requirement: Every AI-visible column must carry the correct data type - amounts as decimal, dates as date, identifiers as whole number - consistently across tables.
rules.rationale: Stated requirement with these exact examples. A numeric amount stored as text cannot be aggregated and the generator will not tell you why the answer is empty.

check.how: Run the Best Practice Analyzer data type rules across AI-visible columns.

rules.remediation: Fix types in Power Query or the source; do not paper over with DAX conversion in measures.
rules.impactIfViolated: Empty or wrong aggregations that look like missing data.

rules.title: Categorical values are standardized
rules.requirement: Values in AI-visible categorical columns must be standardized - Open, Closed, Pending - without mixed case, trailing whitespace, or synonym variants of the same state.
rules.rationale: Data consistency with standardized values is a stated requirement. Instance-value matching is literal; 'open', 'Open ' and 'OPEN' are three different filter targets.

check.how: Profile distinct values per AI-visible categorical column; flag case and whitespace variants of the same value.

rules.remediation: Normalize in the transformation layer and add a data quality test to keep it normalized.
rules.impactIfViolated: Filters match a subset of the rows they should, producing understated numbers that look valid.

rules.title: Format strings are set on AI-visible measures and columns
rules.requirement: Measures and columns must carry appropriate format strings, since format string is part of the grounding data.
rules.rationale: Format strings are listed among the semantic model properties supplied as grounding data in both the data-question and DAX query view paths. They tell the generator whether a number is currency, a percentage or a count.

check.how: List AI-visible measures and numeric columns with empty or default format strings.

rules.remediation: Set currency, percentage and precision formats explicitly.
rules.impactIfViolated: Percentages presented as raw decimals and currency without denomination.

rules.title: Data categories are set where they carry semantic meaning
rules.requirement: Columns representing geography, URLs, images or barcodes must have the appropriate data category set.
rules.rationale: Data category is explicitly part of the grounding data supplied to Copilot.

check.how: Check data category on geographic and URL columns in the AI schema.

rules.remediation: Set City, State/Province, Country and Postal Code categories on the relevant columns.
rules.impactIfViolated: Weaker map visual selection and geographic reasoning.

rules.title: High-cardinality columns are identified and justified
rules.requirement: High-cardinality columns must be identified with the Semantic Model Memory Analyzer and either removed, or justified and excluded from the AI data schema.
rules.rationale: Named as a target of analysis alongside incorrect data types and inefficient DAX. High cardinality drives both model size and the instance-value index budget.

check.how: Rank AI-visible columns by cardinality from a VPAX extract; review the top of the list for necessity.

rules.remediation: Remove, bucket, or exclude from the AI schema. A transaction ID needs no place in a natural-language surface.
rules.impactIfViolated: Index budget exhausted by columns nobody asks about, starving the ones they do.

rules.title: Descriptions exist on every AI-visible table, column and measure
rules.requirement: Every table, column and measure in the AI data schema must carry a description.
rules.rationale: Adding descriptions to tables, columns and measures is a stated requirement so the model can understand purpose. Descriptions are the only place where business meaning reaches the generator.

check.how: Compute description coverage across AI-visible objects via INFO functions or a TMDL scan. Report percentage complete.

rules.remediation: Write descriptions for the AI-visible subset only - which is another reason to keep that subset small.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator maps user language to fields on name similarity alone.

rules.title: The essential content of every description sits in the first 200 characters
rules.requirement: Descriptions must front-load their meaning: only the first 200 characters are used by Copilot, and semantic model property descriptions are truncated at 200 characters.
rules.rationale: This is the single most commonly violated hard limit in Copilot preparation. Teams write thorough 600-character descriptions and two thirds of the content is discarded before the generator sees it.

check.how: For every AI-visible object, measure description length. Flag any description over 200 characters, and manually confirm the first 200 characters are self-sufficient.

rules.remediation: Rewrite so the first sentence carries the definition and the usage note. Treat 200 characters as the whole budget, not a soft target.
rules.impactIfViolated: The disambiguating half of your documentation is silently discarded, and the model looks documented while behaving as if it is not.

limit.description: Only the first 200 characters of a description are used by Copilot.

rules.title: Descriptions state usage guidance, not just a restatement of the name
rules.requirement: Descriptions must add information the name does not already carry - what the measure means, when to use it, what to pair it with, and any caveat.
rules.rationale: The documented model description pattern demonstrates this: it defines the calculation and then states which column to use it with. A description reading 'Total Sales measure' costs 200 characters of budget and adds nothing.

check.how: Sample descriptions and score them for added information beyond the object name.

rules.remediation: Follow the pattern: definition, then usage guidance. For example, year-over-year difference in orders, used with Date[Year] to show years other than the latest.
rules.impactIfViolated: Description coverage looks complete on a report while delivering no disambiguation.

rules.title: Descriptions are prioritized where names are ambiguous
rules.requirement: Descriptions must be present for abbreviated or generic object names, columns holding codes, flags, units or category values, date columns tied to a specific business event, and any object in a large schema.
rules.rationale: This is the documented priority list for where descriptions earn their keep. It gives you an order of work when full coverage is not yet achievable.

check.how: Identify objects in each named category and confirm description coverage on them specifically.

rules.remediation: Work the priority list before chasing blanket coverage.
rules.impactIfViolated: Effort spread evenly while the genuinely ambiguous objects stay undocumented.

rules.title: Synonyms are populated in the linguistic schema
rules.requirement: Business synonyms and alternative phrasings must be registered in the model's linguistic schema for AI-visible objects.
rules.rationale: Field synonyms and the full model linguistic schema are supplied as grounding data. Synonyms are how the generator bridges the gap between how the business speaks and how the model is named.

check.how: Inspect the linguistic schema for synonym coverage on AI-visible objects; flag objects with only the default term.

rules.remediation: Harvest synonyms from actual user questions and support tickets rather than inventing them.
rules.impactIfViolated: Users phrase questions in their own vocabulary and Copilot fails to map it.

rules.title: Q&A is enabled on the semantic model
rules.requirement: Power BI Q&A must be enabled on every semantic model in scope for Prep for AI features and advanced DAX generation.
rules.rationale: Stated as a hard prerequisite: you must enable Q&A on your semantic model. Advanced DAX generation requires the Q&A setting, which is on by default for Import and Direct Lake models but must be verified.

check.how: Check the Q&A setting on every in-scope semantic model.

rules.remediation: Enable Q&A in semantic model settings.
rules.impactIfViolated: Prep for AI features and instance-value-aware DAX generation do not function.

rules.title: Q&A retirement in December 2026 is tracked as a dependency
rules.requirement: The roadmap must record that Q&A retires in December 2026 and that a replacement setting will carry instance value indexing forward, with an owner assigned to track the transition.
rules.rationale: Advanced DAX generation currently depends on the Q&A setting. A dated retirement of a dependency your AI surface relies on needs an owner before the date, not after.

check.how: Confirm the retirement is on the roadmap register with a named owner and review date.

rules.remediation: Add it to the platform dependency register and re-check the replacement setting each quarter.
rules.impactIfViolated: A dated platform change lands unmanaged on a production AI surface.

rules.title: Report visuals carry descriptive titles
rules.requirement: Visuals on reports within the AI surface must have descriptive titles rather than default or decorative ones.
rules.rationale: Preparing report visuals with descriptive titles is a step in the documented implementation workflow, and report metadata from the current page is grounding data for questions about visuals.

check.how: Sample in-scope report pages and review visual titles for descriptiveness.

rules.remediation: Retitle visuals to name the metric and the grain, for example Revenue by Region, Last 12 Months.
rules.impactIfViolated: Weak grounding for visual-level questions and poorer report summaries.

rules.title: Hierarchies are defined for natural drill paths
rules.requirement: Logical hierarchies must be defined for drill-down on the main dimensions - date, geography, product and organization.
rules.rationale: Establishing logical groupings for drill-down is a stated structural requirement.

check.how: List defined hierarchies and compare against the main AI-visible dimensions.

rules.remediation: Define hierarchies and describe them so drill intent is unambiguous.
rules.impactIfViolated: Drill-oriented questions answered at the wrong grain.

rules.title: Refresh timeliness is communicated in metadata
rules.requirement: The refresh schedule and data currency must be stated in the semantic model description or AI instructions.
rules.rationale: Clearly communicating data timeliness through refresh schedules is a stated metadata requirement. Without it, an answer carries no indication of how current it is.

check.how: Confirm data currency is stated in the model description or AI instructions.

rules.remediation: Add a line such as: data refreshes nightly at 02:00 UTC; today's transactions are not included.
rules.impactIfViolated: Decisions made on stale figures presented without qualification.

rules.title: RLS is defined for sensitive data reachable by AI
rules.requirement: Row-level security roles must be defined and assigned for any sensitive data reachable through a Copilot or agent surface.
rules.rationale: Defining role-level access for sensitive data is a stated metadata and security requirement. AI surfaces do not create new security, but they do remove the friction that used to limit exposure.

check.how: Enumerate RLS roles and their assignments for in-scope models; confirm coverage of the sensitive tables identified in the data classification.

rules.remediation: Define the roles, assign the groups, and test with View As before enabling AI on the model.
rules.impactIfViolated: Conversational access to data the user was never intended to see.

rules.title: RLS behaviour is tested through the AI surface itself, not only in reports
rules.requirement: Every RLS role must be tested by asking representative questions through Copilot and through each data agent, not only by validating reports.
rules.rationale: Report-level RLS validation does not exercise the generated-query path. The generator composes queries no report author wrote, and those are the queries whose security behaviour matters here.

check.how: For each role, run the golden question set as a member of that role and confirm results are correctly restricted.

rules.remediation: Add per-role AI testing to the release checklist with recorded evidence.
rules.impactIfViolated: An RLS gap that only manifests on generated queries reaches production undetected.

rules.title: Report metadata sensitivity is assessed before enabling Copilot
rules.requirement: Before enabling Copilot on a report, confirm that report metadata - which can include column values - does not carry data unsuitable for transmission to the AI service.
rules.rationale: Explicit caution: report metadata may contain sensitive data such as column values, and it forms part of the grounding data sent for questions about visuals.

check.how: Review in-scope reports for hard-coded filter values, slicer defaults and titles containing sensitive identifiers.

rules.remediation: Remove sensitive literals from report metadata, or exclude the report from the AI surface.
rules.impactIfViolated: Sensitive values leave the tenant boundary inside grounding data.

rules.title: Agent permission model is understood - read access, not Build
rules.requirement: The agent access design must reflect that a Power BI semantic model source requires only Read permission, not Build, and that the agent operates with the consuming user's read access.
rules.rationale: Stated directly. Teams often assume Build permission gates agent access and design their security around an assumption that does not hold.

check.how: Document the permission required per source type and confirm the access design matches.

rules.remediation: Re-derive the access design from actual permission requirements and re-test with a least-privileged account.
rules.impactIfViolated: Broader effective access than the security design intended.

rules.title: Agents are confirmed read-only against every source
rules.requirement: Confirm and document that agents issue only read queries - no create, update or delete - across SQL, DAX and KQL sources.
rules.rationale: Documented behaviour, and worth recording explicitly because it is the question every security reviewer asks first.

check.how: Record the read-only constraint in the security design and confirm source permissions do not grant write regardless.

rules.remediation: Grant the agent's effective identity read-only permissions at the source as defence in depth.
rules.impactIfViolated: Reliance on application behaviour where a source permission would be the durable control.

rules.title: Non-Fabric consumption paths are assessed for compliance boundary exit
rules.requirement: Where agents are consumed from Microsoft Foundry, Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot or an MCP server, the compliance implication must be assessed and approved.
rules.rationale: Explicit warning: responses consumed from non-Fabric services may be sent outside Fabric's compliance boundary or geographic region, governed by the consuming service's terms rather than Fabric's.

check.how: List every consumption surface per agent and confirm compliance sign-off for each non-Fabric path.

rules.remediation: Restrict external consumption to agents whose data classification permits it.
rules.impactIfViolated: Regulated data leaves the assessed compliance boundary through a surface nobody reviewed.

rules.title: Sensitivity labels are applied and their AI behaviour understood
rules.requirement: In-scope semantic models and reports must carry sensitivity labels consistent with the organization's classification scheme.
rules.rationale: Labels are the mechanism through which downstream protection and DLP decisions are made on AI-surfaced content.

check.how: Report label coverage across in-scope items.

rules.remediation: Apply labels and enforce mandatory labelling on AI-enabled workspaces.
rules.impactIfViolated: No basis for downstream protection decisions on AI output.

rules.title: Object-level security interaction with AI grounding is tested
rules.requirement: Where OLS is in use, confirm through testing how restricted objects behave in Copilot grounding and in generated queries.
rules.rationale: OLS restricts metadata visibility, which interacts with schema grounding in ways that need empirical confirmation on your own model rather than assumption.

check.how: Test as an OLS-restricted user and record whether restricted objects appear in grounding or generated DAX.

rules.remediation: Record actual observed behaviour per model and feed it into the security design.
rules.impactIfViolated: OLS assumptions that do not hold on the AI path.

rules.title: Verified answers exist for the highest-frequency questions
rules.requirement: The most frequently asked and highest-consequence questions in the scope must be covered by verified answers rather than left to generation.
rules.rationale: A verified answer returns a curated visual instead of triggering DAX generation. It is the most direct fix for both latency and correctness on the questions that matter most, and it is the mechanism that stops repeated broad scans for the same recurring question.

check.how: Rank in-scope questions by frequency and consequence; confirm the top tier has verified answers.

rules.remediation: Build verified answers from existing report visuals for the top questions before tuning anything else.
rules.impactIfViolated: Every recurring question re-plans a query from scratch, at full token and scan cost, with non-deterministic results.

rules.title: Each verified answer carries five to seven trigger questions
rules.requirement: Every verified answer should define roughly five to seven trigger questions covering natural variations in phrasing, including both formal and conversational wording.
rules.rationale: Stated explicitly as five to seven trigger questions per verified answer. Too few and the answer never fires; the trigger set is what determines hit rate.

check.how: Count trigger questions per verified answer and review phrasing variety.

rules.remediation: Harvest real phrasings from usage logs and support requests rather than writing variations from imagination.
rules.impactIfViolated: Verified answers exist but rarely fire, so the tuning effort produces no measurable benefit.

rules.title: Verified answers use no more than three filters
rules.requirement: Configure up to three filters per verified answer to keep it flexible for slicing.
rules.rationale: Documented limit of three filters per verified answer.

check.how: Count configured filters per verified answer.

rules.remediation: Where more slicing is needed, create a second verified answer rather than overloading one.
rules.impactIfViolated: Configuration rejected or the answer becomes too narrow to fire.

rules.title: No verified answer references a hidden column
rules.requirement: Verified answers must not reference hidden columns or measures.
rules.rationale: Stated flatly: verified answers will not work if they reference hidden columns. The failure is silent, which makes it expensive to diagnose.

check.how: For each verified answer, resolve referenced objects and confirm none are hidden.

rules.remediation: Unhide the referenced object or rebuild the verified answer on a visible equivalent.
rules.impactIfViolated: Verified answers silently never fire and the team concludes the feature does not work.

rules.title: Verified answers are re-saved after any referenced object is renamed
rules.requirement: Renaming a table, column or measure referenced by a verified answer requires updating and re-saving that verified answer.
rules.rationale: Explicit rule. Renames are routine during model tuning, so this breaks constantly unless it is part of the change process.

check.how: Confirm the model change process includes a verified-answer revalidation step after renames.

rules.remediation: Add verified answer revalidation to the rename checklist and to the release pipeline.
rules.impactIfViolated: A cosmetic rename silently disables the curated answers protecting your top questions.

rules.title: Verified answer authoring prerequisites are met
rules.requirement: Authors creating verified answers in the Power BI service must be in a Copilot-enabled workspace, hold authoring permission on the underlying semantic model, be on a report page in edit mode, with the visual selected.
rules.rationale: All five conditions are documented prerequisites. When the option is greyed out, one of them is unmet - this list is the diagnostic.

check.how: Confirm the authoring team meets all five conditions and that the checklist is in the authoring guide.

rules.remediation: Publish the five conditions in the authoring guide as a troubleshooting checklist.
rules.impactIfViolated: Authors blocked with no visible reason and the capability goes unused.

rules.title: Verified answer coverage is measured against actual question volume
rules.requirement: The proportion of real user questions answered by a verified answer rather than by generation must be measured and tracked over time.
rules.rationale: Coverage is the leading indicator for both cost and consistency. It is also the only way to know whether verified-answer investment is paying back.

check.how: Sample real questions over a period and classify each as verified-answer hit or generated. Report the hit rate.

rules.remediation: Feed the miss list back into verified answer creation each cycle. The threshold here is a working target, not a Microsoft-published figure.
rules.impactIfViolated: No feedback loop; verified answers stay frozen at their initial guess of what users would ask.

rules.title: AI instructions exist and carry business context
rules.requirement: AI instructions must be configured with industry and business context, key terminology definitions, table and field mapping guidance, measure specifications and synonyms, and audience prioritization rules.
rules.rationale: These five content elements are the documented structure. AI instructions influence more Copilot capabilities than any other single configuration - report summary, questions about visuals, questions about the semantic model, create report page, and DAX query.

check.how: Review the AI instructions against the five required content elements.

rules.remediation: Structure the instructions on the documented template, then test with real questions.
rules.impactIfViolated: The generator has no map from business vocabulary to model objects.

rules.title: AI instructions are configured in Prep for AI, not at data agent level, for semantic models
rules.requirement: For semantic model sources, AI instructions must be set in Prep for AI. Data agent level instructions are ignored for semantic model DAX generation.
rules.rationale: Stated as a direct rule. This is a high-frequency configuration mistake: teams write careful agent instructions for a semantic model source and none of it reaches the DAX generator.

check.how: For each semantic model source, confirm the substantive instructions live in Prep for AI and that agent-level instructions contain only cross-source guidance.

rules.remediation: Move semantic model guidance into Prep for AI; keep agent instructions for formatting, routing, abbreviations and tone across sources.
rules.impactIfViolated: Instructions written, paid for in tokens, and ignored by the generator.

rules.title: Instructions are focused and specific rather than long and complex
rules.requirement: AI instructions must be kept focused and specific; conflicting or overly complex instructions must be avoided.
rules.rationale: Documented on two counts: clear instructions are more effective than complex or conflicting ones, and overly complex instructions reduce accuracy while increasing latency. Instructions are also billed as input tokens on every single request, so verbosity has a direct and recurring CU cost.

check.how: Review instruction length and internal consistency; flag contradictory directives and unbounded lists.

rules.remediation: Cut instructions to the rules that changed behaviour in testing. Measure the token cost per request before and after.
rules.impactIfViolated: Higher latency, higher CU burn on every question, and lower accuracy.
